Jacob Coxon, a former employee at the artificial intelligence giants OpenAI and Anthropic, joined protesters outside the latter’s company headquarters Thursday as it traded on the Nasdaq for the first time.

Coxon and about 100 other people gathered outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters to warn about the dangers of AI. Coxon was an Anthropic researcher when he resigned in September, warning that “people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

He added that Anthropic is “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”

Thursday’s protest focused on banning recursive self-improvement, or RSI, which has been used to help train future generations of AI.

“You end up potentially compressing decades of AI research into months, and if we don’t understand the AI, this leads to potentially highly dangerous, highly advanced AI systems by the end of 2027,” Coxon told AFP.

Despite his concerns, Coxon admitted earlier this month that he still has OpenAI equity, where he worked for several years before moving to Anthropic, calling it “blood money.”
